newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins slip on Yeltsin health worries.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins slip on Yeltsin health worries.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds slipped in slow trading on Monday on worries about President Boris Yeltsin's health, a fall in U.S. Treasuries and anticipation of a high U.S. employment cost index, dealers said.

"I cannot say it is a trend, but there is still instability in the U.S. economy and Yeltsin's health still causes fears," an ICFI Moscow Partners dealer said. "Any news about Yeltsin can now push prices down."

Sergei Kovzharov, chief dealer at Moscow Business World Bank, said investors were worried by the fact that Yeltsin, who is now recovering from pneumonia, had not been seen on television for several weeks.
The Kremlin later said Yeltsin had cancelled a visit to the Netherlands due next week on the orders of his doctors.
Besides, banks feared that the fourth quarter 1996 employment cost index, to be issued on Tuesday at 1330 GMT, would be too high and that added to the slip, he said.
"We could feel in the morning that the market was pessimistic and prices did go down in the afternoon," he said.
Kovzharov said the domestic MinFin market had followed the international emerging debt market where Russian debt dropped on Monday.
"The market is nervous and bids are sinking," Kovzharov said, adding he did not see much sales from the West.
